lead: Palantir Technologies / PLTR — the growth bill hits the faithful
smaller: Bitcoin / BTC — digital gold fails the war test
DoorDash / DASH — the pandemic habit that stuck
why_lead: Palantir had the largest single-session drop on the card (-15.75% to 11.77 USD, -19.49% over 20 sessions) on a concrete own-date catalyst, Reuters' report that margins will take a hit from higher spending in the commercial push [[n0941]], and it fell on the day the crowd's whole high-beta book sold off (AFRM -12.23%, SHOP -11.63%, SOXL -11.34%, HOOD -9.33%, ARKK -6.44%) as war fear returned (Biden's very-high-risk warning [[n1532]], US calling the withdrawal claim false [[n1528]], VIX +15.73%). Attention evidence comes from Munger's 'speculative mess' verdict on retail trading apps [[n1869]] and Bloomberg's retail-rebellion segment [[n1885]]; the Smart Money View is genuinely split (Cathie Wood's 'way undervalued' [[n1889]] vs Munger; Temasek adding Robinhood [[n1862]]); the analog pairs the own-date Meta ranking story [[n0929]] with the general spend-now, profit-later repricing mechanism. Relation to strictly earlier retail notes: Palantir has not appeared in any earlier retail note or draft; the Meta precedent is cited only through the new 17 February Bloomberg ranking story, not the crash coverage used on 3, 4 and 8 February.
why_smaller: Bitcoin / BTC: a new crypto narrative, the haven test, on 17 February evidence (separatist shelling [[n1521]]; gold +1.63% to 1,902.00 USD/oz while BTC -7.79% and ETH -7.88%), with Sequoia [[n1067]], Buffett's Nubank stake [[n0828]], the FSB warning [[n1053]] and the Big Short DAO [[n1063]] as the split. Relation to earlier notes: bitcoin led on 8 and 14 February and was a smaller item on 4 February ('the faithful hold while Big Tech bleeds') and 9 February; this edition shows the opposite of the 4 February pattern on new evidence and is kept secondary.

DoorDash / DASH: the pandemic habit that held, with the 17 February session confirming the after-hours beat (CNBC record orders [[n0883]], +10.69% to 105.03 USD). Relation to earlier notes: the 2022-02-17 Shopify lead cited DoorDash's after-hours jump only as a counter-signal; this is the first full item, built on 17 February coverage (n0883, n0884, n0881, n0882, n0853).

Walmart / WMT: the inflation-winner/defensive narrative on its 17 February results (Bloomberg [[n0970]], Modern Retail [[n0971]], NYT [[n0973]], CNBC's shopper warning [[n0974]]), +4.01% on a -2.12% S&P day. Relation to earlier notes: 2022-02-10 ran Chipotle as pricing through inflation and KO as a dividend bunker; Walmart is a different company with a new results catalyst.
considered_not_chosen: Gold / GDX as a separate item (gold 1,902.00 USD/oz, GDX +13.33% over five sessions): gold was a smaller item on 14 and 17 February, so it appears here only as the comparison inside the Bitcoin item.
Roku (revenue miss, shares down 20% after hours [[n0949]]): another growth-miss story close to the Palantir lead and the 17 February Shopify lead.
Shopify (-11.63%, -26.12% over five sessions) and Affirm (-12.23%): continuations of the 17 and 14 February items, used only as card values in the lead's Social Signal.
Intel investor meeting (NYT comeback question n0960, Fast Company on the $43.5B plan n0911): little price reaction (INTC -1.37%) and no clear crowd angle.
Deere results (Barron's preview 'coming Friday' n0150): pending after the cutoff, not used as a trade thesis.
Avoided as possibly after cutoff: no item stamped 18 February is used, and the AP 7,000-troops item (n1503), whose briefing time is uncertain, is not relied on.
